verdict.rationale: Cal.com does publish an MIT-licensed self-hostable edition (Cal.diy) and docs describe removing all enterprise/proprietary code, and a probe confirms a legacy vendor Docker image (v6.2.0) actually boots a full working instance from source/container. However, concrete community evidence contradicts the 'full scheduling engine, self-hostable' claim: users report Cal.com stopped publishing public Docker images for the OSS split, official docs now say the self-hosted edition is 'strictly recommended for personal, non-production use,' features were stripped after promising full self-host parity, and the Cal.diy image had no published tags at time of the runtime probe — a documented bait-and-switch from prior 'full infrastructure ownership' claims. Missing for 10: a working current-release container image for Cal.diy, resolution of the production-use restriction, and confirmation the API/backend (not just UI) is fully self-hostable without paid dependency.
